content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Observation:**

- **Affected plant part:** Banana fruit (fingers/tips)
- **Key visual features:**
  - Green unripe banana fingers on a bunch
  - The **tips (distal ends) of the bananas** show dark brown-to-black necrotic rot
  - The rotted tips have a shriveled, dry, blackened appearance — a classic "cigar end" pattern
  - The decay is localized strictly at the blossom end (tip) of each fruit
  - No leaf lesions, no vascular discoloration, no bunching abnormalities

**Reasoning against other classes:**
- **Anthracnose** — causes sunken dark spots on ripening fruit, not tip-specific rot on green fruit
- **Bunchy Top** — affects leaves (narrow, streaked, bunched appearance), not fruit
- **Cordana Leaf Spot** — causes oval lesions on leaves, not fruit
- **Panama Disease** — vascular wilt causing yellowing and internal browning of the pseudostem, not localized fruit tip rot
- **Yellow and Black Sigatoka** — leaf diseases with characteristic streaks/spots on foliage

**Matching class — Cigar End Rot:**
The black, shriveled necrosis confined to the distal tip of each banana finger is the hallmark of Cigar End Rot (*Trachysphaera fructigena* or *Verticillium theobromae*). The lesion resembles the burnt end of a cigar — exactly what is visible here.
